issues.display_title: Issue #441: Reuse RabbitMQ Connection in PostComplete Worker
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 13/08/26

✅ Implementation: Reuse RabbitMQ Connection in PostComplete Worker

Changes

  • Extracted publishPostSubscribe for publishing the post SID.
  • Added the small channelOpener interface so the function accepts the existing RabbitMQ connection and remains testable.
  • Removed the second amqp.Dial call from the message-processing path.
  • Kept each publish on a short-lived channel and closed that channel after use.
  • Added contextual errors for channel creation, queue declaration, payload encoding, and publishing.
  • Kept logging at the worker call site.
  • Added a focused test verifying that the supplied connection is asked for exactly one channel.

Files

  • src/Worker/PostComplete/PostComplete.go
  • src/Worker/PostComplete/PostComplete_test.go

Verification

go test ./src/Worker/PostComplete -count=1

Git

  • Commit: dc14f09

Problem

The PostComplete worker opens a second RabbitMQ connection when publishing to the add_post_subscribe queue, even though the worker already has an active connection. Repeated connection initialization adds unnecessary resource usage and can exhaust broker connections.

Scope

  • Reuse the PostComplete worker's existing RabbitMQ connection.
  • Open a short-lived channel for publishing to add_post_subscribe.
  • Close the publishing channel after use without closing the worker connection.
  • Preserve the queue name, message payload, and existing worker flow.
  • Return contextual errors for channel creation, queue declaration, JSON encoding, and publishing.
  • Add a focused test proving the supplied connection is used.
  • Add no dependency.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Publishing to add_post_subscribe does not call amqp.Dial.
  • The existing worker connection supplies the publishing channel.
  • The publishing channel is closed after use.
  • Publish failures remain logged by the PostComplete worker.
  • Focused PostComplete tests pass.

issues.display_title: Issue #444: Accept All Supported Post Categories
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 13/08/26

✅ Implementation: Accept All Supported Post Categories

Changes

  • Updated the upper category ID validation bound in EditPostDescription from 3 to 7.
  • Kept the lower bound, default category, validation response, and remaining edit flow unchanged.

Files

  • src/Action/V1/Posts/EditPostDescription.go

Verification

Confirm category IDs 1-7 pass validation and values outside that range return Category ID not valid.

Git

  • Commit: 2e5a607

Problem

EditPostDescription rejects category IDs above 3, while the supported category range now extends through 7.

Scope

  • Change the accepted category ID range from 1-3 to 1-7.
  • Preserve the default category behavior for empty or "0" input.
  • Preserve existing validation responses and edit flow.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Category IDs 1 through 7 are accepted.
  • Values below 1 or above 7 return Category ID not valid.
  • Empty and "0" category IDs still default to category 1.
  • No unrelated post-edit behavior changes.

RESULT 13/08/26

✅ Implementation: Centralize Worker Error Logging

Changes

  • Removed duplicate direct-SQL SaveLogErr functions from LocationGrouping, PostComplete, and UploadPanorama.
  • Replaced their call sites with Functions.SaveLogErr.
  • Changed early UploadPanorama failures to pass "0" when no valid user ID is available.
  • Added parseErrorLogUserID to the shared helper:
    • Empty strings and "0" represent anonymous errors.
    • Valid UUIDs are retained.
    • Invalid non-anonymous values return an error.
  • Added table-driven tests for anonymous, valid, and invalid user IDs.

Files

  • src/Utils/Functions/Functions.go
  • src/Utils/Functions/error_log_test.go
  • src/Worker/LocationGrouping/LocationGrouping.go
  • src/Worker/PostComplete/PostComplete.go
  • src/Worker/UploadPanorama/UploadPanorama.go

Verification

go test ./src/Utils/Functions -count=1
go test ./src/Worker/LocationGrouping ./src/Worker/PostComplete ./src/Worker/UploadPanorama

Git

  • Commit: 6d79306

Problem

LocationGrouping, PostComplete, and UploadPanorama contain local SaveLogErr implementations that write directly to error_log. The duplicate implementations bypass shared validation and make error logging behavior inconsistent.

Scope

  • Remove worker-local SaveLogErr functions.
  • Route worker error logs through Functions.SaveLogErr.
  • Preserve logged URL, payload, response, platform, and available user IDs.
  • Use anonymous user IDs for failures occurring before a valid user is known.
  • Add no dependency.

Acceptance Criteria

  • The three affected workers use Functions.SaveLogErr.
  • No worker-local SaveLogErr implementation remains in those workers.
  • Anonymous worker errors can be saved without parsing "0" as a UUID.
  • Existing worker control flow remains unchanged.
  • Related Go tests pass.

RESULT 13/08/26

✅ Implementation: Allow Anonymous Error Logs

Changes

  • Added a migration dropping the NOT NULL constraint from error_log.user_id.
  • Changed Models.ErrorLog.UserID from uuid.UUID to *uuid.UUID and removed the GORM not null tag.
  • Updated the Save Log API to assign a pointer to the parsed user UUID.
  • Updated shared worker logging to assign nil for anonymous errors.

Files

  • migrations/20260812_make_error_log_user_id_nullable.sql
  • src/Models/ErrorLog.go
  • src/Action/V1/Users/SaveLog.go
  • src/Utils/Functions/Functions.go

Migration

ALTER TABLE error_log ALTER COLUMN user_id DROP NOT NULL;

Git

  • Commit: 6d79306

Problem

The error_log.user_id column requires a UUID, but workers can encounter errors before a user is identified. Existing callers use "0" as an anonymous marker, which is not a valid UUID.

Scope

  • Make error_log.user_id nullable.
  • Update the GORM model to represent a missing user ID.
  • Preserve valid user IDs for authenticated error logs.
  • Update the Save Log API to store its parsed UUID through the nullable model field.
  • Provide a database migration.

Acceptance Criteria

  • error_log.user_id accepts NULL.
  • Models.ErrorLog.UserID is nullable.
  • Anonymous worker errors store NULL instead of an invalid UUID.
  • Authenticated API error logs retain their user UUID.
  • Migration and model definitions agree.

RESULT 13/08/26

✅ Implementation: Initialize Post Processing Flags

Changes

  • Extracted construction of an initialized post into newInitPost.
  • Set IsProcessing and IsUploading to explicit false pointers before GORM creates the row.
  • Preserved IsPublish = false, generated UUID, user ID, slug, and API response flow.
  • Added a focused regression test proving both flags are non-nil and false.
  • Added no migration or backfill.

Files

  • src/Action/V1/Posts/InitAddPost.go
  • src/Action/V1/Posts/InitAddPost_test.go

Verification

go test ./src/Action/V1/Posts -run TestNewInitPostStartsIdle -count=1 -timeout=30s

Git

  • Commit: 7f44fc5

Problem

InitAddPost creates a GORM Models.Post with IsProcessing and IsUploading left as nil pointers. GORM inserts those values as SQL NULL, so the database defaults are not applied. AddPostCompleteV1 then cannot find the post because it requires is_processing = false.

Scope

  • Initialize is_processing to false when creating a post through InitAddPost.
  • Initialize is_uploading to false in the same flow.
  • Do not migrate or backfill existing rows.
  • Preserve the current post ID, slug, publish state, and response behavior.
  • Add a focused regression test.

Acceptance Criteria

  • New posts created by InitAddPost store is_processing = false.
  • New posts created by InitAddPost store is_uploading = false.
  • Neither flag is inserted as NULL.
  • Existing rows remain unchanged.
  • Focused post tests pass.
